summary: Kodo Kawamura (1933–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Komazawa University from circa 1951 to 1956, where he later served as a professor from circa 1978 to 2003.

Kodo Sawaki (1880–1965) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka (~1908–1912). He was a professor at Komazawa University (~1935–1953) and taught Kosho Uchiyama, Sodo Yokoyama, and Gudo Wafu Nishijima.
Kodo Yamada (1867–1939) worked in Buddhist studies and held teaching positions at Komazawa University and Keio University.

Koen Wellens specializes in sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kvaerne.
Koenraad Elst (born 1959) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his MA at KU Leuven (circa 1986–1998) and studied at Banaras Hindu University from circa 1988 to 1992.

Kogen Mizuno (1901–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning doctorates from the University of Tokyo (~1925–1928) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He taught at Keio, Komazawa (serving as vice president in 1940), and the University of Tokyo (1959–1962).

Kogi Kudara (1945–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested as professor in 1979 and attested in 1997) and the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono (born 1944) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University (attested there in 1995), later serving as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Shinohara (born 1941) works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University (~1972–2004), coordinator at the University of Toronto Mississauga (attested 2004), and Senior Lecturer at Yale University (~2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi (born 1968) specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Tokyo by 2004, studying under Akira Saito and Yasunori Ejima, and held research posts there attested in 2005 and 2015.

Koichi Yokoyama (1940–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973) under Akira Hirakawa and traditional teacher Gyoin Hashimoto, and served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1978–2005).

Koji Kamioka (1938–2024) studied Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics at Kyoto University (~1957–1966) under Yutaka Ochihara. He held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1972–1975) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies as assistant professor (~1975–2001).

Koji Takahashi (1934–2023) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University from circa 1953 to 1957. He later served there as an assistant professor (~1968–1974) and professor (~1974–2005).

Kojun Fukui (1898–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Waseda University (~1920–1925), later holding a post there (~1928–1969), and served as president of Taisho University from circa 1964 to 1970.
Kojun Saito (1930–2002) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He held a post as lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita (born 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki (1931–2008) specialized in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960), where he later served as assistant professor (~1969–1975), department chair (~1975–1997), and director and professor (~1997–2002).

Koken Unno (born 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nagoya University, where he was also an assistant. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music and was a professor at Meijo University (~1986–2007).
Koki Kawagishi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University, both attested in 1976.

Konrad Klaus (born 1956) works in Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn from circa 1980 to 1985 and held a post at the University of Bonn from circa 1993 to 2021, teaching Bruno Galasek.
